newsitem.title: UK: Gilts end touch higher after benign earnings.
newsitem.headline: Gilts end touch higher after benign earnings.

text.p: UK gilts ended 3/32 higher but off the session's highs on Wednesday as the market remained cautious amid renewed fears of a delayed single currency, analysts said.
The market earlier received a boost after average earnings figures for April remained steady and a much smaller-than- expected fall in unemployment in May.

"It has been a very quiet day, with little volume traded. The market was relieved average earnings were not above 4.5 percent, and the unemployment figures were just about okay," a senior gilts salesman said.
The September gilt futures contract closed 3/32 higher at 113-19, in the middle of the day's range which saw gilts rise to a high of 113-26.

The next main focus will be Thursday's May retail price data, with analysts expecting headline RPI to rise to 2.5 percent in the year to May compared with 2.4 percent in April. The figures are due out at 0830 GMT.
Targeted underlying inflation is forecast to stay steady at 2.5 percent.
Analysts attribute the rise in headline inflation to a squeeze in seasonal food prices and higher housing costs.
Bunds were hit by a fresh bout of uncertainty that European economic and monetary union would start on time in 1999.
EU political leaders gather in Amsterdam at the weekend when they had been due to ratify the stability pact which will impose fines on countries running high budgetary deficits once EMU starts.
But ratification at Amsterdam now looks unlikely after the new French government said on Monday it needed time to consult parliament before signing up.
September short sterling settled 0.01 up at 93.09, still comfortably factoring in a quarter point interest rate rise by the end of the third quarter.
